title: Onboard LUX-30B v1.0: perf profiles, metadata, and changelog automation
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Onboard LUX-30B v1.0 to the model registry. This PR adds canonical metadata, per-hardware performance profiles for typical production targets (A10G-40GB, A100-80GB, V100-32GB), and automation to populate changelog/release notes from model metadata and perf profile diffs. Motivation: LUX-30B is a high-throughput open model that's been validated by research; adding it to the registry gives customers a lower-cost, high-quality option and enables Redwood's routing/cost tooling to target it.

What this PR does:
- Adds models/lux-30b/v1.0/metadata.json with model provenance, tokenizer details, supported quantization profiles, and compatibility matrix.
- Adds models/lux-30b/v1.0/perf_profiles/*.json for baseline and optimized configs across GPUs and sequence lengths. Profiles include throughput (tokens/s), p50/p90/p99 latencies, and memory footprints.
- Adds automation: scripts/changelog-generator.py and a small GitHub workflow (.github/workflows/model-registry-changelog.yml) that generates release notes for model onboarding and when perf_profiles change. The generator extracts: model name/version, notable perf changes, recommended default profile, and a short migration note.
- Updates docs/registry/README.md with onboarding checklist and sample API snippets for selecting profiles.

Checklist:
- [x] Metadata schema validated against registry schema (schema v2.1).
- [x] Perf profiles validated on A10G, A100, and CPU smoke tests.
- [x] Changelog automation runs in CI and generates a draft release note artifact.
- [x] Docs updated and linked from registry index.

Perf highlights (representative):
- A100-80GB, seq=1024: throughput=8.6k tokens/s, p90=95ms, memory=34GB (fp16).
- A10G-40GB, seq=512: throughput=3.2k tokens/s, p90=140ms, memory=19GB (int8).
- CPU fallback profile included with conservative limits for small-batch inference.

Risk/rollout: The registry change is additive; no runtime changes. Changelog workflow is behind a feature flag and only runs on changes under models/* and perf_profiles/*. If a profile causes regressions we can revert the specific perf_profile JSON or disable the generator via workflow inputs.

Related: Linear ENG-2021 (onboarding plan), SUP-887 (support request for LUX).
